text: Suddenly the saddle slipped off. <break time="0.8s" /> And fell to the road. <break time="0.8s" /> But Ichabod held on tightly. <break time="0.8s" /> To Gunpowders neck. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeing the church bridge ahead. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> If I could only reach that bridge. <break time="0.8s" /> I would be safe. <break time="0.8s" /> He crossed it and looked back. <break time="0.8s" /> Expecting the rider to vanish. <break time="0.8s" /> In a flash of fire. <break time="0.8s" /> As Brom had said. <break time="0.8s" /> Instead the rider stood up in his stirrups. <break time="0.8s" /> And threw his head. <break time="0.8s" /> Straight at Ichabod. <break time="0.8s" /> It struck Ichabods head. <break time="0.8s" /> And he fell into the dust. <break time="0.8s" /> While the dark rider rushed past. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a whirlwind. <break time="0.8s" /> The next morning. <break time="0.8s" /> Gunpowder was found eating grass. <break time="0.8s" /> At his masters gate. <break time="0.8s" /> But there was no sign of Ichabod. <break time="0.8s" /> By the brook. <break time="0.8s" /> People found his hat. <break time="0.8s" /> And close beside it. <break time="0.8s" /> Lay a pumpkin. <break time="0.8s" /> Broken into pieces. <break time="0.8s" /> Ichabod never returned. <break time="0.8s" /> And years later. <break time="0.8s" /> An old farmer said. <break time="0.8s" /> He had become a judge. <break time="0.8s" /> In a faraway place. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon after Brom married Katrina. <break time="0.8s" /> And whenever the pumpkin was mentioned. <break time="0.8s" /> He laughed in a knowing way. <break time="0.8s" /> But the old wives of the valley. <break time="0.8s" /> Still say that the Headless Horseman carried Ichabod away. <break time="0.8s" /> That night.
